skill.name: github-oauth-nango-integration
skill.description: Guides implementation of GitHub OAuth login and GitHub App repository access through Nango using separate connections and webhooks.
skill.summary: Guides a two-connection Nango setup for GitHub login, GitHub App repository access, and webhooks.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: All static findings were false positives caused by Markdown backticks, TypeScript examples, placeholder URLs, and placeholder secret names. No prompt injection, malicious command execution, credential exfiltration, or reconnaissance intent was found. Semantic review found two implementation safety issues in the examples: browser localStorage token storage and non-constant-time webhook signature comparison.

remediation.suggestion: Recommend HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies or a hardened in-memory token flow. Document XSS tradeoffs if localStorage remains an option.

remediation.issue: Webhook signature comparison uses regular string equality
remediation.suggestion: Use constant-time comparison, such as timingSafeEqual, after validating signature format and equal buffer lengths.

static_findings.snippet: Implements dual-connection OAuth pattern: one for user identity (`github` integration), another for
1. **Login flow** → User authenticates → Store user identity + `nangoConnectionId`
2. **Repo flow** → Same user authorizes app → Store repos + link via `ownerId`
| Repo Access | `github-app-oauth` | PR operations, file access | `repos.nangoConnectionId` |
| Using same connection for login and repo access | Use two integrations: `github` for login, `githu
| Not handling org approval pending | Check for 403 error, set `pendingInstallationRequest` flag |
| Missing `endUser.id` in connection | Always set in `createConnectSession`, update after user creat
| Polling wrong connection ID | Store `incomingConnectionId` separately for returning users |
| Not verifying webhook signature | Always verify `X-Nango-Signature` with HMAC-SHA256 |
- App ID, Private Key, Client ID/Secret: From GitHub App
- Building apps that need both user auth and repo access

semantic_findings.title: JWT Stored in Browser Local Storage
semantic_findings.description: The frontend example stores the issued JWT in localStorage after login. Tokens in localStorage are exposed to JavaScript and can be stolen if the application has an XSS flaw.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly calls localStorage.setItem with the auth token. This is a common but risky browser token storage pattern, with impact dependent on XSS exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Non-Constant-Time Webhook Signature Comparison
semantic_findings.description: The webhook example compares the received Nango signature and expected HMAC with regular string equality. Signature checks should use constant-time comparison after validating length and format.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The comparison is shown as a direct inequality check in the webhook verification sample. This is a real implementation weakness, though exploitability depends on deployment details.

content.value_statement: GitHub login and repository access often require separate OAuth flows. This skill shows a Nango two-connection pattern with webhooks, database mapping, and sync handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains why GitHub OAuth login and GitHub App repository access need separate Nango integrations.
Provides database table patterns for users, repositories, and GitHub installations.
Shows backend route examples for login sessions, app sessions, and polling status.
Describes Nango auth and sync webhook handling for GitHub data.
Includes frontend connection flow examples using the Nango Connect UI.
Lists Nango dashboard setup steps for OAuth App and GitHub App integrations.
limitations: It is guidance and sample code, not a complete installable authentication package.
Examples require adaptation for the user's framework, database layer, and auth middleware.
It assumes Nango, GitHub OAuth App, and GitHub App credentials already exist.
It does not include production tests, migrations, or complete error handling.

use_cases.title: Add GitHub sign-in
use_cases.description: Implement a Nango login flow that stores GitHub user identity separately from repository authorization.

use_cases.title: Connect repositories after login
use_cases.description: Add a GitHub App authorization flow that maps selected repositories back to the authenticated user.

use_cases.title: Process Nango webhooks
use_cases.description: Design webhook handlers that reconcile auth events, sync repository data, and handle pending organization approvals.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the auth flows
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the GitHub login flow and repository connection flow for my app. Include the required Nango integrations and stored identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Design the data model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose tables for users, repositories, and GitHub installations. Explain which Nango connection ID belongs in each table.

prompt_templates.title: Implement webhook handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft the Nango auth and sync webhook logic for GitHub OAuth and GitHub App repository access.

prompt_templates.title: Review production readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my GitHub OAuth and Nango implementation. Check connection separation, webhook verification, token handling, and organization approval behavior.

output_examples.input: I need users to sign in with GitHub and later connect repositories.
output_examples.output: A two-flow plan that uses one Nango GitHub integration for identity and one GitHub App integration for repository access.

output_examples.input: I need to store Nango connection IDs correctly.
output_examples.output: A storage map that keeps the login connection on the user record and the repository access connection on repository records.

output_examples.input: I need to handle GitHub organization approval delays.
output_examples.output: A webhook and polling strategy that records pending approval and returns a waiting state until repositories are available.

best_practices: Keep login identity and repository access in separate Nango integrations.
Verify every Nango webhook signature before parsing or processing the payload.
Store installation and repository ownership data so access can be reconciled after syncs.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse the user login connection for repository operations.
Do not ignore pending organization approval when a GitHub App installation returns limited access.
Do not store temporary connection IDs as permanent repository access records.

faq.question: Why are two Nango integrations needed?
faq.answer: GitHub OAuth identifies the user, while a GitHub App grants repository access. The skill links both flows through the user record.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples that must be adapted to an existing application.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover webhook security?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Nango webhook signature verification, but production code should use constant-time comparison.

faq.question: Can it handle organization approval delays?
faq.answer: Yes. The flow records pending installation approval and lets the frontend show a waiting state.

faq.question: Does it include Nango dashboard setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists the OAuth App, GitHub App, webhook URL, and sync configuration steps.
